I sold my business for $66 million. He went out of business about three years later.

When I turned 35, I made my first real profit at The Corcoran Group. There was more than $40,000 left in the account at the end of the year, and I could hardly believe it. Until then, I’d put every penny we made right back into the business.

That afternoon, I was riding down the West Side Highway when I spotted a car dealership and told the taxi driver to pull over. I walked into the showroom and pointed to the smallest car, figuring it would be the cheapest.

“What’s that cute brown car in the corner?”

“A 911 Carrera.”

“That’s the brand?”

“No, ma’am. It’s a Porsche.”

“How much?”

“About $40,000.”

“I’ll take it!”

The salesman looked stunned. He told me I’d have to pay before I could drive it out, so I came back that afternoon and drove home in my brand-new Porsche. 

I figured I’d find somewhere to park it later.

I spent the next month grinding the gears before I noticed people looking at me as I drove by. That’s when I decided I needed an outfit to match. 

Here I am in my first real leather jacket and my first real cashmere headband. I figured my usual pants would do.

It’s time to ignite a spark for a new season of entrepreneurs stepping into the Tank! 🦈⚡️
